statement: Mechanism comparison: the idea as originally stated is largely covered by existing work. 'Semantic score plus temporal term in a hybrid ranking' is the published three-signal BM25+dense+exponential-decay framework; 'learnable temporal scoring with explicit validity checking' is Chronofy; 'hard as-of/point-in-time gating with a temporal-evidence-leakage metric' is TempFinRAG; and 'temporal validity in a legal benchmark' is LEGAL-LINK-EU. The differences that remain are packaging and measurement, not mechanism: post-hoc application so the base retriever is untouched (Chronofy instead modifies representation and retrieval layers), a hard valid-time gate rather than learnable decay, clause-version identity as the gold label rather than MCQA options, and a cross-retriever interaction test that no reviewed work runs. Treating the temporal term as the contribution would therefore be an implementation-level difference.

evidence.quote: We propose a three-signal hybrid framework integrating BM25 lexical matching, dense semantic embeddings, and exponential temporal decay, which achieves 99.8% temporal accuracy and 50.8% entity precision across all three languages
Layer 2 integrates learnable exponential decay functions into graph-based retrieval
